commonErrors.example: A learner writes on the worksheet that every molecule in a gas heated from 300 K to 600 K now moves faster than it did before.

fixIt.corrected: Hotter means a higher average: the whole spread of speeds shifts up, but some molecules still crawl.
fixIt.prompt: Fix it: state what actually happens to the spread of molecular speeds when a gas is heated, and what happens to the slowest molecules.

commonErrors.misconception: In a hotter gas every molecule moves faster.

commonErrors.example: On the exit ticket, a learner picks the statement that every molecule moves faster than before when a gas is heated.

fixIt.corrected: The average speed rises, but some molecules are still slow
fixIt.prompt: Fix it: explain in one sentence why a hotter gas still contains some slow molecules.

commonErrors.misconception: In a hotter gas every molecule moves faster.

modelAnswers.answer: Atoms at the hot end vibrate with larger amplitude and collide with their neighbours, passing kinetic energy along atom by atom through the lattice; in a metal, free electrons also carry energy rapidly through the rod. No atoms travel the length of the rod - the energy is relayed, and the far end warms as its atoms gain kinetic energy.
modelAnswers.question: One end of a metal rod is held in a flame. A minute later the far end feels warm. Explain, at the particle level, how the energy got there.

modelAnswers.answer: The pressure grows by a factor of 450 / 300 = 1.5, because at fixed volume p is proportional to the kelvin temperature: hotter molecules collide with the walls harder and more often.
modelAnswers.question: A sealed gas at 300 K is heated to 450 K at fixed volume. By what factor does its pressure change, and why?

nextSteps: Reteach the every-molecule-faster trap from the paired notes trap before any further thermal work: temperature tracks the average kinetic energy only.
Practise stating average and spread explicitly whenever a temperature change is explained at the particle level.
strengths: Most of the class can state that the pressure of a sealed gas doubles to 2.0 x 10^5 Pa when it is heated from 300 K to 600 K at fixed volume on the worksheet.
The class can name conduction as the mechanism that warms the top of a metal spoon handle standing in hot soup on the exit ticket.
